description: Frontend: rewrite OrderService and LabelingService to call the live FastAPI backend (environment.apiUrl + Bearer from auth.getToken()) instead of mock JSON, and wire the dashboard and labeling consumers to the new Observables with pixel<->normalized conversion and basic error states. Depends on FEAT-001 (LabelingService.saveLabeling calls PUT /orders/{id}/labels). Keep YOLO detection, auth, the chart's StatusChartService, and the grid columns working. Do NOT delete the JSON asset files; services just stop reading them.
steps: Rewrite src/app/services/order.service.ts: inject AuthService, import environment. Keep the camelCase Order interface (grid depends on it: orderId/orderType/orderStatus/comment/user/imageUrl/accuracy/label). Add a private authHeaders(): HttpHeaders reusing the detection.service.ts pattern (Bearer when token exists). Add private mapOrder(o: any): Order mapping snake_case OrderOut -> camelCase: orderId=o.order_id, orderType=o.order_type, orderStatus=o.order_status, comment=o.comment ?? '', user=String(o.user_id ?? ''), accuracy=String(o.accuracy ?? ''), label=o.label ?? '', imageUrl = split comma-separated o.image_urls (null-guarded) into an array, prefixing paths that start with '/uploads' or are otherwise server-relative with environment.apiUrl (leave http(s):// and assets/ paths untouched). Implement getLabelOrders(): Observable<Order[]> = GET `${environment.apiUrl}/orders` with authHeaders, piped map(list => (list ?? []).map(o => this.mapOrder(o))). Provide getOrders() as an alias to the same mapped list. Add getStats() GET /orders/stats, getOrder(id) GET /orders/{id} (mapped), createOrder(body) POST /orders, updateOrder(id, body) PUT /orders/{id}, all with authHeaders. Remove ordersUrl/jsonUrl fields and the assets JSON reads.

Rewrite src/app/services/labeling.service.ts: inject AuthService, import environment, add the same authHeaders() helper. Update interfaces: keep LabelBox {x,y,w,h,label} and add optional confidence?: number and image_path?: string. Add a StoredBox interface matching backend DetectionOut-ish {label, confidence, x, y, width, height, image_path} (normalized). Add an UploadResult interface {filename, original_name, url, size, content_type}. Remove jsonUrl, getLabelingData(), and the fake-labels.json read. Implement getLabelsByOrderId(orderId): Observable<StoredBox[]> = GET `${environment.apiUrl}/orders/${orderId}/detections` with authHeaders, piped map(list => list ?? []) (caller converts normalized->pixel). Implement saveLabeling(orderId, labels): Observable<any> = real PUT `${environment.apiUrl}/orders/${orderId}/labels` with authHeaders, body = normalized box list [{label, confidence, x, y, width, height, image_path}] (remove the setTimeout stub). Implement uploadImage(file: File): Observable<UploadResult> = real POST `${environment.apiUrl}/uploads/single` with FormData field 'file' and authHeaders (do NOT set Content-Type manually); remove the setTimeout stub.

Update src/app/dashboard/dashboard.component.ts: keep the getLabelOrders().subscribe({next,error}); add an errorMessage: string field set in the error handler, distinguishing err.status === 401 ('Session expired. Please log in again.') from other errors ('Could not load orders from the server.'). Optionally surface errorMessage via a small *ngIf block in dashboard.component.html.

Update src/app/labeling/labeling.component.ts: inject LabelingService. After images are resolved and the canvas is sized, call labeling.getLabelsByOrderId(this.orderId).subscribe and convert each stored NORMALIZED box to pixels into boxes[currentImageIndex] ({x: b.x*canvas.width, y: b.y*canvas.height, w: b.width*canvas.width, h: b.height*canvas.height, label: b.label}), guarding non-finite values exactly as runDetection() does, then drawBoxes(); set a loadError string on failure (401 vs generic). Rewrite saveLabeling() to persist for real: read boxes[currentImageIndex], require canvas.width>0 && canvas.height>0, convert px->norm ({label: b.label, confidence: 1, x: b.x/canvas.width, y: b.y/canvas.height, width: b.w/canvas.width, height: b.h/canvas.height, image_path: this.images[this.currentImageIndex] ?? ''}), and call labeling.saveLabeling(this.orderId, normBoxes).subscribe({ next: set a saveMessage success flag, error: set a saveError (401 vs generic) }). Remove the alert()/console.log mocks. Keep runDetection() (YOLO) and all manual-drawing handlers unchanged; keep cancel() clearing the current image's boxes.

If needed for the new fields, add minimal *ngIf error/success spans in src/app/labeling/labeling.component.html (near the existing detectionError span) for loadError/saveError/saveMessage, and in src/app/dashboard/dashboard.component.html for errorMessage. Do not restructure existing markup.
acceptance_criteria: `cd /Users/irfan/Downloads/DashBoard-GenAI-master && npx ng build --configuration development` compiles with no TypeScript or template errors (strict + strictTemplates).
order.service.ts and labeling.service.ts contain no references to assets/orders.json, assets/LabelsOrders.json, or assets/fake-labels.json, and no setTimeout stubs remain.
Both services build request URLs from environment.apiUrl and attach Authorization: Bearer via auth.getToken(); no hardcoded URLs or tokens.
The dashboard grid still binds the Order interface fields used by order-columns.ts (orderId/orderType/orderStatus/label/user/accuracy/comment) and renders without template errors.

labeling.component.saveLabeling() calls LabelingService.saveLabeling with normalized boxes (not alert/console mocks), and existing labels load back and render as pixel boxes; the 'Run YOLO Detection' button and manual drawing still work.
A backend-down or 401 response sets an observable error field in both the dashboard and labeling components instead of throwing uncaught.
detection.service.ts, auth.service.ts, and status-chart.service.ts are unchanged; the JSON asset files still exist on disk.
verification: grep for assets/orders.json, assets/LabelsOrders.json, assets/fake-labels.json, and setTimeout in src/app/services/order.service.ts and src/app/services/labeling.service.ts and confirm none remain (sanity check, not the primary gate).

With FEAT-001's backend running on :8000 and a logged-in session, manually confirm the dashboard table populates from GET /orders and the labeling page loads existing detections and successfully PUTs edited labels (optional live check; the build is the required gate).
